products.name: Jamf AI Governance
products.note: Native AI control plane for macOS fleets, GA July 1, 2026; discovery and policy enforcement for on-device and cloud AI use on Mac endpoints

reading.body:
Jamf's AI Governance product is a control plane for managing AI use on Mac fleets, covering both on-device and cloud AI applications through discovery and policy enforcement across enterprise endpoints.

Most AI governance products focus on data centers or cloud deployments. Jamf addresses a different layer: the endpoint itself, the Mac computers where employees actually run AI tools. This matters because enterprise security has historically centered on network perimeter and server-side controls. As AI models move onto local devices, the security model must shift with them. Discovery and policy enforcement at the endpoint level become the enforcement point for what AI workloads are permitted, where data flows, and what compute resources are consumed.

For an AI infrastructure thesis centered on compute and power, endpoint governance is a secondary concern, not a primary constraint. Jamf does not build data centers, power systems, or chips. It manages the consumption side: which employees can use which AI models, on which machines, under which policies. This affects how efficiently an organization deploys AI, but not whether the grid or real estate can support it. A company with abundant local compute on its Macs may still be constrained by Jamf's policies. A company constrained by global chip supply will not be freed by better governance.

The data does not cover Jamf's customer base, adoption rates, or whether enterprises are actually using this product to restrict or enable AI use on their fleets. It shows only that the product exists and when it reached general availability.

profile_text.body:
Jamf, founded in 2002 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, describes itself as a provider of enterprise Apple device management and security software. The company's platform covers management, connectivity, and cybersecurity for Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Vision Pro devices, serving organizations ranging from small businesses to large enterprises. Jamf describes itself as having over 20 years of experience and claims an unmatched reputation for same-day Apple OS support, and IDC MarketScape has positioned the company in the Leaders Category for Worldwide Unified Endpoint Management Software for Apple Devices in its 2025–2026 vendor assessment.

On the AI side, Jamf tracks a product called Jamf AI Governance, categorized as an AI Governance and Risk Management Platform. The company describes it as a native AI control plane for macOS fleets, providing discovery and policy enforcement for on-device and cloud AI use on Mac endpoints, with general availability set for July 1, 2026.

The site's held facts show that Jamf has the heaviest legal exposure concentration in Minnesota, with 136 associated cases, though no specific litigation details are recorded. No MCP server registrations or SEC filings are noted in the available data.
